lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: conflict de-escalation and repair

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic conflict de-escalation and repair task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With a trusted adult's guidance, the learner picks one real, low-stakes disagreement with someone in their own household (such as a chore, a shared space, or a scheduling conflict), plans the conversation using the three-part structure, has the real conversation with that household member, and the trusted adult confirms afterward that it happened and stayed respectful.
safetyNotes: This task is only appropriate for a genuinely low-stakes disagreement (such as a chore, shared space, or schedule); it is never used for a conflict involving anger that feels unsafe, a pattern of ongoing mistreatment, or any topic a trusted adult advises against revisiting.
The trusted adult decides whether the identified disagreement is appropriate to revisit before the learner starts; if it is not, the learner uses the role-play alternative instead.
No recording of the conversation is made or required; the trusted adult confirms based on their own knowledge or a short conversation with both people afterward.

simulationAlternative.description: If no real disagreement is currently available, or a trusted adult judges an available one is not appropriate to revisit, the learner instead role-plays the entire repair conversation with the trusted adult using a realistic fictional scenario (such as a sibling leaving a shared space messy), taking both the three-part planning step and the full spoken conversation just as seriously as the real version, with the trusted adult giving the same confirmation of respectful delivery at the end.

materials: adult-or-local: a trusted adult who confirms the conversation afterward

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: What is one thing you would say differently if you had this same kind of conversation again, and why?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u05-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Conversation planning and follow-through: Plan names the disagreement without blame, includes the learner's own part, proposes one specific next step, and the learner completes either the real conversation or the role-play alternative. | Repair quality as confirmed by the trusted adult: The trusted adult confirms the conversation (or role-play) happened and stayed respectful on both sides. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner plan and have a second repair conversation about a separate low-stakes disagreement with a different household member, this time also asking that person one specific question about how the disagreement affected them before proposing the next step.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic conflict de-escalation and repair task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

localMaterials.label: a trusted adult who confirms the conversation afterward
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: conflict de-escalation and repair worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With a trusted adult's guidance, the learner picks one real, low-stakes disagreement with someone in their own household (such as a chore, a shared space, or a scheduling conflict), plans the conversation using the three-part structure, has the real conversation with that household member, and the trusted adult confirms afterward that it happened and stayed respectful.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact conflict de-escalation and repair decision or action.
Model move 2: Identify one real, low-stakes disagreement you've had recently with someone in your household, and check with a trusted adult that it's an appropriate one to revisit.
Model move 3: Plan your repair conversation using the three-part structure: name the disagreement without blame, state your own part in it, propose one specific next step.

Model check: Conversation planning and follow-through: Plan names the disagreement without blame, includes the learner's own part, proposes one specific next step, and the learner completes either the real conversation or the role-play alternative. | Repair quality as confirmed by the trusted adult: The trusted adult confirms the conversation (or role-play) happened and stayed respectful on both sides.

resources.title: conflict de-escalation and repair action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for conflict de-escalation and repair.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.

resources.title: conflict de-escalation and repair coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With a trusted adult's guidance, the learner picks one real, low-stakes disagreement with someone in their own household (such as a chore, a shared space, or a scheduling conflict), plans the conversation using the three-part structure, has the real conversation with that household member, and the trusted adult confirms afterward that it happened and stayed respectful.
Coach direction: Identify one real, low-stakes disagreement you've had recently with someone in your household, and check with a trusted adult that it's an appropriate one to revisit.
Learner prompt: Describe the disagreement in one or two neutral sentences, without assigning blame.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: conflict de-escalation and repair complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Plan your repair conversation using the three-part structure: name the disagreement without blame, state your own part in it, propose one specific next step.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My opening names the disagreement using 'I' language rather than starting with an accusation.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I named one specific thing I could have done differently, not just what the other person did.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I proposed one specific, doable next step, not a vague promise like 'I'll try to do better.'

Equal-access rule: If no real disagreement is currently available, or a trusted adult judges an available one is not appropriate to revisit, the learner instead role-plays the entire repair conversation with the trusted adult using a realistic fictional scenario (such as a sibling leaving a shared space messy), taking both the three-part planning step and the full spoken conversation just as seriously as the real version, with the trusted adult giving the same confirmation of respectful delivery at the end.

resources.title: conflict de-escalation and repair minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What is one thing you would say differently if you had this same kind of conversation again, and why?

Success checks: Conversation planning and follow-through: Plan names the disagreement without blame, includes the learner's own part, proposes one specific next step, and the learner completes either the real conversation or the role-play alternative. | Repair quality as confirmed by the trusted adult: The trusted adult confirms the conversation (or role-play) happened and stayed respectful on both sides.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: conflict de-escalation and repair supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u05-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional conflict de-escalation and repair condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Conversation planning and follow-through: Plan names the disagreement without blame, includes the learner's own part, proposes one specific next step, and the learner completes either the real conversation or the role-play alternative. | Repair quality as confirmed by the trusted adult: The trusted adult confirms the conversation (or role-play) happened and stayed respectful on both sides..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
